findings.title: deploy/rollback.sh cannot roll back across any migration, and takes the site down trying
findings.mechanism: `up -d` starts the migrate and search-migrate one-shots (the api/search services depend on them with service_completed_successfully). Their `migrate up` runs on the PREVIOUS release's image, whose embedded migrations stop below the ledger. internal/dbmigrate's Up() has no branch for 'the ledger is ahead of the newest embedded migration': golang-migrate returns a not-exist error for the current version, it falls into the default case, and the one-shot exits 1. Every dependent service is then never started.
findings.blast_radius: every rollback across any migration — i.e. every rollback anyone would want. Both ledgers, both services (vidra-search carries its own copy of the same logic; the identical error appeared for version 18).
findings.why_ci_misses_it: vidra-core's schema-compat workflow runs the previous release tag's TEST SUITE against HEAD's schema. It never runs the previous release's MIGRATOR against that schema, which is what `up -d` does.
findings.aggravating: rollback.sh's `up -d` is not `|| die`-guarded, so set -e kills the script before its readiness probes and before the 'THE ROLLBACK TARGET IS ALSO UNHEALTHY / restore the pre-deploy dump' trailer the operator needs. They get a raw compose error and a dark site.
findings.proposed_fix: in vidra-core (and the same in vidra-search) internal/dbmigrate.Up(): read the ledger first, and when its version exceeds the newest embedded migration, log loudly ('the database is at N, this binary ships migrations up to M — assuming a deliberate rollback; not migrating') and return nil. That is exactly the state the one-release compat policy calls supported. Needs a ruling: no-op-and-log versus refuse-with-a-better-message.
findings.not_fixed_here: a meta-side workaround would have to enumerate services for `up -d --no-deps`, which re-introduces the drift deploy/lib.sh exists to prevent. Left for the architect.

findings.title: the documented incompatible-schema recovery order re-applies the migration it is escaping
findings.mechanism: rollback.sh's header and deploy/README.md say: stop api/frontend, restore.sh <pre-deploy dump>, rollback.sh <previous tag>. restore.sh runs BOTH migrators after reloading the dump, using the tags currently in the env file. Run it with the tags still on the new release and the destructive migration is simply re-applied. Run it after rollback.sh has rewritten the tags and the old migrator refuses the restored ledger (finding A38-1) — proven in run 13, with the database already dropped and reloaded.
findings.consequence: exactly one pairing works — a dump whose schema the pinned release's migrator can reach — and neither script checks it. Run 14 is that pairing.
findings.proposed_fix: state the pairing rule in deploy/README.md and have restore.sh compare the dump's schema_migrations version against the pinned image's `migrate version` before it drops anything. Fixing A38-1 removes most of the sharp edge.

findings.title: `vidra doctor` could never report a dirty ledger
findings.mechanism: the schema-ledger check ran `docker compose exec -T api migrate version`. `exec` replaces the container's command and does not prepend the ENTRYPOINT, so it asks for a binary called `migrate`; there is none, and /app is not on PATH. On every bundled-Postgres deployment the check failed with exec-not-found and reported 'the database is unreachable from the api container', pointing the operator at a healthy Postgres.
findings.proven: on the run-8 stack, whose ledger really was 137 dirty, the shipped doctor said 'the database is unreachable'; `exec -T api /app/api migrate version` in the same container answered `version=137 dirty=true`. The patched doctor reports 'the core migration ledger (schema_migrations) is DIRTY at version 137' with the force runbook.
findings.status: FIXED — vidra-core PR #191. The unit fake matched the broken argv with a loose Contains; it now matches the real command, and a new test asserts both the argv and the Dockerfile ENTRYPOINT it is copied from (verified to fail on the pre-fix argv).

findings.title: the release images could not be deployed from anywhere but ghcr.io
findings.mechanism: docker-compose.prod.yml hardcoded `ghcr.io/${VIDRA_IMAGE_OWNER:-yegamble}/...`, every prod service carries `pull_policy: always`, and deploy.sh step 2 is a bare `pull` gated on its exit code — so an image absent from GHCR could not be deployed even when already present on the host. That blocks an air-gapped or private-mirror operator (the same operator deploy/make-bundle.sh exists for) and it blocks this rehearsal.
findings.status: FIXED here — `${VIDRA_IMAGE_REGISTRY:-ghcr.io}` on the six image references, documented in env/production.env.example. The full --profile core --profile frontend render of the filled template is byte-identical before and after.

findings.title: deploy.sh's health probes cannot see a schema/binary mismatch
findings.detail: run 10 exited 0 with /readyz, the frontend and the edge all 200 while GET /videos/{id}/comments answered 500. The probes prove the processes are alive, not that the release works. Worth saying so where operators read them.

findings.title: a rehearsal image must carry a semver-shaped tag
findings.detail: deploy.sh's require_embedded_migrate_tag refuses any VIDRA_CORE_TAG / VIDRA_SEARCH_TAG that is not vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, so a plain `a38-rehearsal` tag is rejected before anything is touched. A prerelease suffix passes (semver_ge strips it), which is why this lab used v0.6.3-a38rehearsal. Correct behaviour; worth knowing before an operator tries to rehearse.

findings.title: editing deploy/Caddyfile.local with an atomic rename breaks the mount under Docker Desktop
findings.detail: reload_caddy compares the container's copy against the file and force-recreates when the bytes differ — but only when `exec caddy cat` SUCCEEDS. On virtiofs a renamed-over bind-mount source leaves the path dangling, `cat` fails, and the loop treats it as 'caddy is not up yet', sleeps five times and dies. deploy.sh exited 1 while the edge was in fact serving. On Linux the container keeps the old inode and `cat` succeeds, so the existing branch handles it; recreating the caddy container cleared it here.
